raw: {"mode":"iff","restated":"∃ (u₀ : ℝ³ → ℝ³) (f : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³), InitialVelocityConditionPeriodic u₀ ∧ ForceConditionPeriodic f ∧ ∀ (v : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³) (p : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ), ¬ NavierStokesExistenceAndSmoothnessPeriodic nu u₀ f v p","proof":"simp only [not_exists]","english":"For every viscosity nu > 0 there are a smooth, divergence-free, 1-periodic initial velocity u₀ and a smooth, 1-periodic forcing f (with the stated decay in time) such that for every candidate pair (v, p), the pair fails to be a smooth, 1-periodic solution of the Navier–Stokes equations with data (nu, u₀, f).","why_clearer":"It replaces the negated existential with an explicit universal statement, so the breakdown reads as 'no pair (v, p) works'."}

parsed.english: For every viscosity nu > 0 there are a smooth, divergence-free, 1-periodic initial velocity u₀ and a smooth, 1-periodic forcing f (with the stated decay in time) such that for every candidate pair (v, p), the pair fails to be a smooth, 1-periodic solution of the Navier–Stokes equations with data (nu, u₀, f).
parsed.why_clearer: It replaces the negated existential with an explicit universal statement, so the breakdown reads as 'no pair (v, p) works'.
